title: Shape Evolution and Dynamics of Deformable Ring
authors: Arun Kumar, Partha Sarathi Mondal, Pritha Dolai, Shradha Mishra
abstract: We numerically investigate the dynamics of a deformable closed ring filled with active particles. The ring is modeled as a flexible boundary made up of passive beads interacting with a harmonic spring force. The interior of the ring is filled with active Brownian particles (ABPs), and their activity is controlled through the rotational diffusion coefficient. We explore how, by systematically varying the activity of ABPs, packing fraction, and size of the ring, we can control the shape deformation and dynamics of the ring. At low packing fractions, low rotational diffusion coefficients, and smaller ring sizes, the ring exhibits highly irregular and strongly deformed shapes due to the uneven spatial arrangement of active particles along the boundary. Increasing the packing fraction, rotational diffusion coefficient, or ring size promotes a more even distribution of active particles within the ring, thereby suppressing shape deformations and fluctuations, driving the ring toward a more circular shape. We further analyze the mean-squared displacement (MSD) of the ring's center of mass and observe a crossover from ballistic to diffusive dynamics, which can be tuned by varying the system parameters. Our results demonstrate that, despite its internal complexity and deformability, the ring exhibits emergent behavior analogous to that of a single effective active particle. This study provides insight into the collective effects of confined active matter and the resulting macroscopic dynamics of deformable systems.
summary: This paper numerically investigates the collective dynamics of active particles confined within a deformable ring structure. By controlling parameters like particle density and activity, the researchers show that the internal activity drives the ring towards a more stable, circular shape. The study successfully models the emergent center-of-mass motion, demonstrating that the complex internal activity can be accurately described by an effective single-particle model.
main_problem: The study investigates how the internal dynamics of active particles confined within a deformable ring influence the ring's overall shape evolution and macroscopic center-of-mass motion.
main_result: The ring's shape is stabilized and driven towards a circular configuration by increasing the packing fraction, rotational diffusion coefficient, or the number of boundary beads. Furthermore, the collective activity generates emergent dynamics analogous to a single effective active particle.
method: The research employs numerical simulations using Langevin dynamics for both the passive boundary beads and the active Brownian particles, supplemented by analytical derivations for Mean-Squared Displacement (MSD) based on effective particle models.
model_or_system: The system consists of a deformable closed ring formed by passive beads connected by springs, filled with Active Brownian Particles (ABPs). The dynamics are governed by coupled Langevin equations incorporating harmonic, repulsive, and active self-propulsion forces.
key_observables:
Asphericity parameter ($\Delta(t)$), Mean-Squared Displacement ($	ext{MSD}$) of the center of mass, and effective diffusion coefficients ($D_{eff}, 
u_r$).
important_parameters: Rotational diffusion coefficient ($D_r$), packing fraction ($\phi$), number of beads ($N_{	ext{beads}}$), and self-propulsion speed ($v_0$).
main_assumptions: The system is modeled using overdamped Langevin dynamics, and the collective motion is successfully mapped onto an effective Self-Propelled Particle (SPP) model for analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate shape transformations under varying parameters ($N_{	ext{beads}}$, $\phi$, $D_r$), show the probability distribution $P(\Delta)$ for shape fluctuations, and compare the MSD of the full ring simulation against the effective SPP model.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the dynamics by first defining the full coupled particle model, then quantifying shape fluctuations using the asphericity parameter, and finally deriving the effective large-scale dynamics (MSD) by treating the ring as a single effective active particle.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete example of how non-equilibrium active matter can generate collective, macroscopic behavior (like directed motion or shape stabilization) from local particle interactions, which is a key area of modern statistical physics.

Fig. 1(i) illustrates ring configurations for different ro- tational diffusion coefficients, Dr = 0.01, 0.03, 0.05, and 0.07, arranged from Fig. 1(i)(a-d) respectively. In these figures, the packing fraction is kept fixed at ϕ = 0.1, and the ring consists of Nbeads = 100 beads. As Dr increases, the orientations of the active particles randomize more rapidly, reducing the persistence of the propulsive forces exerted on the ring. Consequently, the active particles are unable to introduce significant force in a particular direction, resulting in a weaker ring deformation.
